reader.requirement: At --std 85, for a Format 2 RECORD IS VARYING clause, every record description of the file whose minimum character-position count (GR5: elementary items, redefinitions and renamings excluded, ODO tables at minimum occurrences) is below integer-2, or whose maximum (ODO at maximum) is above integer-3, must be refused; with FROM or TO alone only the stated bound applies; descriptions exactly at the bounds are legal.

edition-consulted.switches: edition.DialectLevel >= Since; both SR4 rows (lower and upper) carry Since 85, so they apply at 85
citation text only: Of1985 VII.3.8.3 SR2 below 2002

reader.edition-search: Read Screen and the Rules table whole; the predicates (MinBytes < Lower, MaxBytes > Upper) are edition-free.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb721 below-minimum / above-maximum witness two plain records; ODO minimum/maximum, REDEFINES exclusion, a second record description, and FROM-only / TO-only clauses are covered by the probes

probes.printed: COBOL2010 x5 citing ANSI §1985:VII.3.8.3 SR2: F1 'R1 describes 5 to 20 bytes, fewer than integer-2 = 6'; F2 'R2 5 to 20 bytes, more than integer-3 = 19'; F3 'R3B describes 11 bytes' (REDEFINES not counted) > 10; F4 (TO only) R4 12 > 10; F5 (FROM only) second record R5B 3 < 4
LEN 08 AAABBB (ODO record 5..20 and a 30-position-with-REDEFINES record under FROM 5 TO 20 accepted; write 8 positions, read back 8)
probes.expected: accepted at the bounds; GR11 sets data-name-1 to the record length read

probes.printed: Stack overflow in StorageFormPass.Classify at --std 85 and --std 2023, also with the RECORD clause removed (so_redef_norec.cob); a single-record FD with the same REDEFINES compiles (so_redef_one.cob)
probes.expected: a legal FD whose SECOND record contains a REDEFINES compiles; this is kb/Work PB5729, independent of the RECORD clause

citations.check: OK  §1985:VII.3.8.3 SR2  (3.8.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR2
OK  §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR5  (3.8.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR5

reader.notes: The screen implements both obligations as two rows at every edition, cites the 1985 rule at 85, and its message body keeps 2023 wording ('bytes'). A REDEFINES in the second or later FD record crashes the compiler before the screen runs (PB5729, already filed; not this rule's defect, it crashes without any RECORD clause).
reader.known_note: PB5729 (the REDEFINES-in-later-record crash met while probing)

refuter.evidence: refute-1985-063/rec2_r.cob --std 85: SD S1 VARYING FROM 6 TO 20 with a 5-position record refused COBOL2010 'fewer than integer-2 = 6'; SD S2 FROM 1 TO 4 with 5 refused 'more than integer-3 = 4' (the rule reaches sort-merge files and the screen does too); FD F1 FROM 9 TO 10 with a 10-position record plus 66 RN1 RENAMES R1A THRU R1B accepted (renamings excluded per GR5). rec2_sync.cob (01 R1: X + 9(9) COMP SYNC under TO 5) accepted and the record file holds a 5-byte record (od: 05 00 00 00 41 00 00 00 07), so the screen and the storage agree on no implicit synchronization FILLER. cite.py: OK §1985:VII.3.8.3 SR2; OK §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR5 'plus any implicit FILLER due to synchronization'.
